reproduction_target: Re-analysis of six previously published nascent-transcription datasets (GRO-seq/PRO-seq: triptolide and flavopiridol in mouse v6.5 cells; TBP degradation in HAP1; ZNF143 depletion in HEK293T; dexamethasone in A549/U2OS/C7; heat shock in Drosophila S2) plus a kinetic 'compartment model' that infers fold changes in initiation rate, pause release rate, and the premature-termination/pause-release ratio from pause-region and gene-body RNA polymerase densities. Computational chain: GEO download -> general PRO-seq/GRO-seq processing pipeline (cited) -> DESeq2 sizeFactor normalization -> Hsp70 consensus construction (bedtools getfasta, clustalw, Biopython dumb_consensus) -> primaryTranscriptAnnotation TSS/TTS definition -> pause-window and gene-body density estimation -> tanh saturation fit with Scipy curve_fit to convert densities into occupancies -> compartmentModel (polcomp) rate inference and figure generation -> UCSC Genome Browser track hubs. No wet-lab experiment is performed in this study; all data are re-used from prior publications, so W = 0.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the bioRxiv v2 JATS XML Methods section (retrieved by curl; WebFetch of the .source.xml returned HTTP 403). The Methods section is largely mathematical derivation of the compartment model (Eqs. 1-20); the tool-level computational chain is compressed into a handful of sentences ('analyzed the raw data using a general pipeline (47, 48)'). The Data Availability statement points to a PyPI package (compartmentModel) and a GitHub Pages vignette (guertinlab.github.io/compartment_model). Per Stage-1 protocol the repo landing page (github.com/guertinlab/compartment_model) and the vignette were consulted at PROSE level only, to fix the capture_claim; the vignette's shell/R code was not read line-by-line. What the landing-page/vignette prose does establish is: install is an unpinned 'python3 -m pip install compartmentModel'; the processing pipeline uses HPC 'module load cutadapt / seqtk / bowtie2 / bedtools / samtools / bamtools / genometools' with no version arguments and hardcoded absolute paths under /home/FCAM/rmukherjee/; there is no lockfile, conda environment file, Dockerfile, release tag, or archival DOI. Every version axis in this report is therefore 0. No wet-lab steps exist; W = 0.

steps.label: Acquisition of the six re-analyzed nascent-transcription datasets from Gene Expression Omnibus — accession numbers are not enumerated in the main text, only stated to be in Table S1; no download script or checksum in prose

Raw read processing and alignment with 'a general pipeline (47, 48)' — no tool, no version, and no parameter is named anywhere in the Methods prose; the pipeline is delegated entirely to two cited references
Within-dataset signal normalization using sizeFactors from DESeq2 — no DESeq2 version, no R version, no normalization script cited in prose

Treatment-specific normalization for the universally repressive treatments: DESeq2 controlGenes taken from read counts over gene regions >50 kb (triptolide, 12.5 min) and >100 kb (flavopiridol, 25 min), justified by a 4 kb/min elongation-rate upper bound — thresholds stated, versions absent

Extraction of six Hsp70 gene sequences (Hsp70Aa/Ab, Hsp70Ba, Hsp70Bb, Hsp70Bbb, Hsp70Bc) plus 50 bases upstream from the BDGP6.46 (release 112) reference with bedtools getfasta — reference release is pinned, bedtools version is not
Multiple alignment of the six Hsp70 sequences with clustalw — no version, no alignment parameters (gap penalties, matrix) stated
Derivation of the Hsp70 consensus sequence with Biopython's dumb_consensus() at threshold 0.6 — threshold stated, Biopython version and Python version absent

Drosophila heat-shock branch: align all S2 data to the Hsp70 consensus, map the remaining unmapped reads to dm6, count reads within genes, normalize replicates with DESeq2 sizeFactors, then restrict to the 249 curated activated genes of Duarte et al. Table S2 and the 65 HSF-dependent genes at FDR < 0.001 — aligner and counting tool are not named, no versions

Definition of the most prominent transcription start site and the inferred transcription termination site with the R package primaryTranscriptAnnotation — no version, no parameters, no annotation input file version stated

Pause-region and gene-body density estimation: maximum-sum 50 bp window within 200 bp of the primary TSS (300 bp for GRO-seq); gene body = 500 bp downstream of the pause window to the inferred TTS or the distance travelled at 2 kb/min, whichever is shorter; flavopiridol bodies capped at 50 kb; triptolide bodies quantified over a 4 kb window starting 1 kb downstream of the pause region — window geometry fully stated, implementing code version unpinned

Conversion of densities into absolute occupancies: hyperbolic-tangent fit y = A*tanh(B*x) + C to log-transformed ranked pause sums with Scipy optimize.curve_fit, saturation = A + C used as maximum occupancy for UMI-containing datasets, 90th-percentile pause sum used for datasets without UMIs, all densities then scaled 0-1 — no Scipy version, no initial guesses, bounds, or RNG/optimizer settings stated

Compartment-model rate inference with the compartmentModel Python package (polcomp): fold change in pause release (Eq. 8), bounds on fold change in initiation (Eqs. 11-12), and the premature-termination / pause-release ratio (Eqs. 16-17) parameterized by Y in [0,1], with elongation rate assumed constant between conditions in the 1800-4000 bp/min range — model equations fully specified in prose, package installed unpinned from PyPI

Steady-state validation fits: exponential decay a*e^(-b*x) + c fitted to the published triptolide initiation time-series with the slope evaluated at t = 12.5 min, and dexamethasone long-gene analysis demarcating affected / transition / unaffected regions on genes >150 kb using 85 activated genes and 85 length- and expression-matched unchanged genes — fitting tool, matching procedure, and versions not stated

Generation of UCSC Genome Browser track hubs and the browser snapshots used in Fig. S4D-I — mentioned only in the Data Availability pointer to the vignette; no tool, version, or track-generation parameter in the Methods prose

headline.static_readiness: 0/14 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: NI on 12/14 computational steps and X on 2/14. Not a single software version number appears anywhere in the Methods prose, in the Data Availability statement, or on the repository landing page: the install instruction is an unpinned 'python3 -m pip install compartmentModel', and the processing pipeline is invoked through HPC 'module load' statements with no version arguments. The version axis is therefore 0 for every step, which caps every step at NI and rules out RI entirely at Stage 1. Two steps fall to X on the params axis: the upstream read processing and alignment, which is delegated wholesale to two citations without naming a single tool or parameter, and the UCSC track-hub generation, which is not described at all. What the paper does well is the mathematical layer - the compartment model is fully derived in prose (Eqs. 1-20) and the analysis geometry (50 bp pause window, 200/300 bp search region, 500 bp offset, 2 kb/min body-length cap, 0.6 consensus threshold, tanh saturation form, 90th-percentile fallback) is stated precisely enough to reimplement. Reproducibility here is limited by environment and version capture, not by conceptual under-specification.
headline.coverage: 14 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v2 JATS Methods plus the Data Availability statement. W = 0: the study performs no wet-lab work and re-uses six previously published GRO-seq/PRO-seq datasets, so there are no out-of-scope physical steps.

gaps.missing: No version number is stated for any software anywhere in the paper: DESeq2, bedtools, clustalw, Biopython, primaryTranscriptAnnotation, Scipy, R, Python, and the compartmentModel package itself are all named without versions. The Data Availability statement instructs 'python3 -m pip install compartmentModel', which resolves to whatever the latest PyPI release happens to be at install time, so the analysis code itself is a moving target.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact version of every tool and library in Methods, and pin the analysis package to a specific released version (e.g. 'compartmentModel==X.Y.Z') in the Data Availability statement.

gaps.missing: No lockfile, conda environment file, container image or digest, or requirements.txt with pins is claimed in the paper, on the repository landing page, or in the vignette prose. The vignette's own processing script relies on site-specific HPC 'module load cutadapt; module load seqtk; module load bowtie2; module load bedtools; module load samtools; module load bamtools; module load genometools' with no version arguments, plus hardcoded absolute paths under /home/FCAM/rmukherjee/, which makes the environment non-portable even to a reader who follows the vignette exactly. capture_claim is 'floating'.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a lockfile (pip-tools / conda-lock / pixi) or a container with a recorded digest covering the full toolchain, and replace 'module load' plus absolute site paths with a portable environment specification and relative or configurable paths.

gaps.where: Steps C2, C14 (params = 0); secondarily C1, C3, C6, C9
gaps.missing: The upstream read processing and alignment is described only as 'analyzed the raw data using a general pipeline (47, 48)' - no adapter sequence, trimming threshold, aligner, genome index, deduplication or UMI handling, or signal-generation setting appears in the Methods. UCSC track-hub generation has no description at all. Secondary under-specification: no clustalw alignment parameters, no primaryTranscriptAnnotation parameters, no DESeq2 call details, and no curve_fit initial guesses or bounds.
gaps.how_to_close: Enumerate the processing pipeline parameters inline in Methods (or reproduce the exact commands in a Methods supplement), and state all non-default arguments and any RNG seeds for the fitting steps.

gaps.where: Data Availability statement and Table S1
gaps.missing: No GEO/SRA accession number is enumerated anywhere in the main text; the reader is referred to Table S1 ('Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) accession numbers for datasets used in this study'), a supplementary table that is not part of the retrievable full text. The Data Availability statement itself contains only the PyPI URL and the vignette URL - it says nothing about data. In addition, no intermediate artifact (normalized bigWigs, pause/body density tables, per-gene rate estimates) is deposited, so the model layer cannot be re-run independently of a full reprocessing of six raw datasets.
gaps.how_to_close: List the GEO accessions explicitly in the Data Availability statement, and deposit the derived pause-sum / body-density / rate tables (one file per dataset) so the compartment-model layer can be reproduced without re-running the upstream pipeline.

gaps.missing: There is no separate Code Availability statement; code is reachable only through the Data Availability paragraph. The analysis code lives at github.com/guertinlab/compartment_model (200 OK) and on PyPI, but the landing page shows no release tag, no version history, no archival DOI (Zenodo / Software Heritage), and no citable snapshot. Nothing ties the published figures to a specific commit, so a future reader cannot recover the state of the code as used for this manuscript.
gaps.how_to_close: Cut a tagged release corresponding to the manuscript, archive it to Zenodo for a DOI, and cite that DOI in an explicit Code Availability statement alongside the PyPI package name and version.

gaps.where: Steps C11 (occupancy calibration) and C8 (Hsp70/HSF gene selection)
gaps.missing: The occupancy calibration involves recorded human judgement: the authors 'evaluated both untransformed and log-transformed ranked pause sums and attempted to fit several saturation functions' before selecting the log-transformed tanh fit, and 'manual inspection of genes with high pause signals' was used to attribute the observed uptick to multicopy and non-uniquely-mappable genes. The 90th-percentile fallback for non-UMI datasets is an explicitly acknowledged approximation that the authors themselves show is not supported for the Drosophila heat-shock dataset (Fig. S3B-C). Neither the discarded candidate fits nor the manual inspection outcomes are recorded as artifacts.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the fit-selection comparison (candidate functions, transformations, resulting saturation values per dataset) and the list of genes excluded or flagged by manual inspection, so the calibration decision is auditable rather than narrated.

gaps.missing: No out-of-scope wet-lab work exists: the study is a pure re-analysis plus kinetic modelling of six previously published datasets, so W = 0 and the entire pipeline is in scope for computational reproduction. This is recorded for completeness, not as a deficiency.
